correctness.rationale: The global upper bound and equality analysis reconstruct correctly. Radial expansion reduces to cyclic quadrilaterals. For a cyclic quadrilateral, the four edge-normal widths reduce after the stated cyclic/reversal relabeling to a minimum equal to \(a q\). Writing the relevant half-arcs as \(s\le t\) gives \(w=\sin s\,\sin(s+t)\). If \(s\le\pi/4\), this is already below the target; if \(s\ge\pi/4\), then \(t\ge s\) and monotonicity of sine past \(\pi/2\) gives \(w\le\sin s\sin(2s)=2\sin^2s\cos s\), whose unique maximum is attained at \(\sin^2s=2/3\) with value \(4\sqrt3/9\). Equality forces \(s=t=\arcsin\sqrt{2/3}\), and the remaining arc inequalities give exactly the stated one-parameter family. The triangle bound is strictly smaller. A fresh independent numerical replay over fifty thousand random cyclic quadrilaterals stayed below the constant and reproduced the complete displayed equality family to machine precision; this finite replay is corroborative only.
residual_risks: The theorem is only the four-vertex disk problem; larger even vertex counts remain outside the claim.
